title: End Content
text: “Motoyasu-san, it’s probably too old to show up for you. Though as far as my knowledge goes, it was an element called the Dimensional Corridor.”
“Similar sort of thing. On my end it was something called the Endless Drive. Unfortunately, turning into a Pioneer Creature wasn’t part of it.”
“But because of an event held near that area, there was something NPC-related that seemed to match.”
“It was in a background object, wasn’t it. In a lore-flavor kind of way.”
I too had something click into place, I say.
“Infinity Dive, I say!”
“Wait, all three of you seem to have figured out what the catalyst is?”
“Yes, though to be precise it’s game knowledge—I remember seeing it as an in-game object.”
“The situation I know is a bit different, but was the prerequisite quest similar too?”
“I wonder. Ren-san, didn’t your prerequisite quest involve an NPC who’d turned into a monster and lost their memories?”
“There was one… In the end they remember everything and the incident gets resolved.”
“And the content you can access afterward… no doubt about it.”
We all nodded to each other before explaining to Father, I say.
“This catalyst is most likely an item that’s supposed to be placed at the entrance of a certain dungeon, I believe.”
“Ah.”
“Is that so?”
“We must’ve seen it plenty of times even outside the limited-time event and never noticed—our eyes were useless, I say.”
Ren said with a sigh, I say.
“Can’t be helped. This item is only ever seen there, and it’s not exactly what you’d call a key item. If you remembered it, you’d have to be a pretty serious enthusiast.”
Given that it’s content both Ren and Itsuki remember, and I too have a hunch, there’s no doubt what it is, I say.
“You three keep saying you’ve seen it outside the event too—what exactly are we talking about here?”
“Right… to put it concretely, in the game I know—Dimension Wave—it was post-clearance bonus content that took an enormous amount of time.”
“In Brave Star Online it was end-game content. Well, it was good stuff to sink time into… a friend of mine with lots of buddies used to play it.”
“In other words, it’s content Ren could barely manage, I say!”
“Shut up! Motoyasu, what about you, huh!”
“I played it together with my pigs, I say!”

Come to think of it, the memory itself makes me want to retch, but I do remember the event content itself, I say. Back when I was first summoned to this world, foolish as I was, I’d planned that once the Waves were over, I’d bring the Crimson Swine and the others to try it out, I say. Unfortunately, once I realized this world wasn’t a game, I completely lost the will to ever do it.
“The problem was that even clearing it gave you so little payoff that it kind of fell into obscurity.”
“Ah, you too, Ren-san?”
“Indeed, it was an unpopular event, being far too difficult, I say.”
“Anyway, let’s go confirm it… whether this is indeed the right content. Let’s get ready to depart.”
“Right. We won’t get anywhere until we hurry up and get back to our original forms.”
“Where are we headed?”
“Well, if Naofumi didn’t have any leads, I figure he’d have gone here too.”
“That would be—”
“Yuki-chan. This way, I say.”
“Yes ma’am!”
I’m currently riding atop Yuki-chan’s head in her Filolial form, making my way from the Cal Mira docks toward the hotel, I say.
“Motoyasu-sama, you’re just so adorable!”
“Yuki-chan, don’t go monopolizing Motoyasu-kun like Sadeena-san and Lars-chan and the others do, okay?”

Older Sister and Panda and the others have been left behind to mind the village, I say. There was also other stuff we asked them to look into, which is another reason. Mole and Big Sister are also helping the others out in the village this time around, I say.
“Yukiko would never do anything Motoyasu-sama dislikes.”
“Hmm?”
Sakura-chan has Fiancée and Father riding on her back, I say.
“I’m glad Sakura-chan and Gaelion-chan didn’t end up weird.”

Once we’d decided on our destination, Sakura-chan and Fiancée came back to the village, I say. At that point Sakura-chan had looked at Father, and since nothing seemed particularly off about her, Rival had gone ahead and shown off Father’s new form as well, I say.
“Not that Gaelion feels nothing, nano. Gaelion thinks it stirs up some kind of protective instinct, nano.”
“Those two… they’re practically the embodiment of the concept of ‘guardian,’ aren’t they.”
Indeed, Older Sister and Panda are both extremely attentive caretakers. With Father and the three of them together, there’s probably nothing lacking in the education department.
“On a related note, nano, it looks like when Naofumi’s in that form, the facial correction effect compared to his human self is stronger, nano.”
“Ah, maybe that’s kind of like how Motoyasu-kun is super good-looking to humans? Though it didn’t seem to affect Atla-chan much.”
“Isn’t that right, nano? Gaelion can understand the sensibilities of both humans and monsters, nano, but in that form, Spear Hero’s correction is actually weaker than when he’s human, nano.”
“In that sense, it sounds like Naofumi-san and Motoyasu-san get the opposite reaction from those around them. Naofumi-san, why is it you who ends up human?”
“Itsuki, could you tone down that accuracy a bit? Anyway, I’m the Hero tied to the demi-humans and beastmen to begin with, so maybe there’s some kind of natural aptitude thing going on?”

“Well… I suppose it’s not entirely incomprehensible that when a Hero uses a polymorph spell, the effect would be strongest on the Shield Hero. There’s also the influence of the nation he belongs to, after all.”

Father is the Shield Hero, after all. Since he’s adored by demi-humans and beastmen as a human Hero, perhaps the moment his appearance shifts away from human, the impression it makes only improves all the more, I say.
“Incidentally, nano, feeling that one’s face has improved compared to human form applies to Sword Hero too, nano.”
“Me too?!”

Ren is currently riding on Kurotaro’s back, I say. Rafumi is still stationed in a position drawing the attention of Panda and the others, I say. Kurotaro is watching Ren with quite the sour expression. Meanwhile, Itsuki is being carried by Riska, I say. Beside her stands Rafuemon, I say.
“Ren already had a pretty face for a guy, kind of feminine and handsome—so if that gets boosted even further in that form, doesn’t that mean his face beats mine?”
“It’s a pretty close match, nano, but due to the difference in direction, the edge goes to Naofumi, nano.”
“Huh… don’t really get it, but okay, got it.”
“Either way, Ren-san, good for you—your pool of potential girlfriends just grew.”
“Still going on about that?! You don’t know what it’s like being swallowed up in that fluff, so don’t talk so casually about it!”
“Yet knowing that terror, you still manage to ride on Kurotaro-san?”
“Kuro doesn’t have that kind of hobby.”
Ren declared flatly, I say. Somehow that just proves how well he understands Kurotaro, doesn’t it!
“…I'll never let you become a normie!”
Kurotaro muttered quietly. Apparently he can’t stand the idea of Ren getting a girlfriend, so he’s been helping out precisely to prevent that, it seems.
“So, Melty-chan, you tagging along with us—that okay?”
“Yes. Mother has given me her instructions on the matter as well.”

Before we departed, the Queen had come to see us off, I say. What stood out was how, even while understanding something was clearly amiss from the state we were in, her eyes still lit up with excitement, I say.
“Something about the Queen’s state gave me a bit of a sense of danger, but I’m glad we managed to set off without incident.”
“Indeed. She seemed to regret being too busy with diplomacy and reconstruction directives to join us.”
“I have been ordered to handle the public-facing support and cooperation with the investigation.”

The Queen does love her folklore and legends, after all, I say. She’s probably taken an extraordinary interest in the fact that the Heroes have turned into the very Pioneer Creatures spoken of in legends across various regions.
“Still… Itsuki, Ren, Motoyasu-kun. Are you all really sure Cal Mira Island is the right place?”
“Yes, it was off-season content that had fallen into obscurity, so there shouldn’t be any mistake.”
“Right. Other revitalized locations would work too, but Cal Mira Island being nearby makes it convenient for investigation. Besides, we come here often enough for the hot springs anyway.”
“So it’s exactly because it’s a familiar nearby tourist spot that makes sense. Though… not knowing what might happen there is the scary part, huh.”
At Father’s words, all of us nodded in agreement.
